title.en: Temperature, the Kelvin scale and thermal equilibrium
Why does a hot tea cool down?

text.en: A cup of hot tea cools and a cold bottle warms until both match the room. Energy flows from hot to cold, never the other way, until they reach the same temperature. That is thermal equilibrium, and the Kelvin scale lets us measure it from absolute zero.

Temperature is the degree of hotness of a body, a scalar quantity that decides the direction of heat flow; its SI unit is the kelvin (K).
Thermal energy or heat flows from a hot body to a cold body because of the temperature difference, and it is the agent that produces the sensation of warmth.
The Kelvin scale is the absolute or thermodynamic scale: K = C + 273, and zero kelvin equals -273 degrees Celsius.
A difference of 1 degree Celsius equals a difference of 1 K; one kelvin is 1/273.16 of the triple point of water.
Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium if there is no net flow of thermal energy between them, which means they are at the same temperature.
Heat flows until the temperatures of the bodies become equal.
Temperature measures hotness; heat is the energy transferred, so they are not the same thing.

problem.en: Convert 27 degrees Celsius to kelvin and 300 K to Celsius.

text.en: To go back use C = K - 273, so 300 - 273 = 27 degrees Celsius.

prompt.en: Define temperature, heat and thermal equilibrium and state the SI unit of temperature.

requiredIdeas.en: Heat flows from hot to cold

commonMisconceptions.en: Using temperature and heat as the same thing

points.en: Temperature: degree of hotness; SI unit kelvin.
Heat flows from higher to lower temperature.
At thermal equilibrium temperatures are equal and net flow stops.
